newsitem.title: USA: Traders surprised by latest cert coffee stock draw.
newsitem.headline: Traders surprised by latest cert coffee stock draw.

text.p: A steep decline in U.S. certified coffee stocks reported on Monday surprised many traders, and could boost prices in a market already unnerved by low levels of supplies.
U.S. certified coffee stocks plummeted 24,391 60-kg bags, or more than 80 percent, in the week ended October 18, to 5,583 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said.
In addition, no coffee was reported pending certification, greatly diminishing chances for an equally sharp build next week, traders said.
Traders had anticipated a slight decline in certified coffee stocks in line with small drawdowns seen in recent weeks. A week ago, CSCE stockpiles fell by 750 bags, to a 12-year low of 29,974 bags.
"It is a shock," a trader said. "We certainly did not expect an increase but neither did we expect a 20,000-bag decrease. It should make the market short-term excited."

With concerns about near-term supplies mounting, traders said the nearby switch stands to benefit the most by the draw. December's premium to March ballooned to 8.95 cents Monday, compared with 7.55 cents Friday.
"Watch out for the switch tomorrow," another dealer said. "Anyone short has to be concerned about their position."
The latest drawdown in coffee stocks comes ot a time when U.S. consumer stocks, comprising both exchange-deliverable and non-exchange coffee, are hovering at their lowest levels in almost a decade.

Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses were reported at 1.6 million bags in September, their lowest level since the Green Coffee Association, an industry trade group, began tracking inventories in 1988.
"There is not enough coffee around and the drop in certified stocks is just a confirmation of this," one trader said.
But some traders, noting sharp gains racked up on the futures exchange Monday, said the latest drawdown may have already been factored into the market.
"It seems as if the market would react on the positive side, but we may have seen some of it absorbed in the marketplace today," one analyst said.
CSCE December coffee ended up 3.90 cents a lb, to 113.00 cents on Monday, while March coffee closed 2.50 cents higher, at 104.05 cents.
